newsitem.title: USA: TVA to offer $300 million in inflation-linked bonds.
newsitem.headline: TVA to offer $300 million in inflation-linked bonds.

text.p: The Tennessee Valley Authority said Tuesday it became the first U.S. private entity to sell inflation-indexed bonds with the sale of $300 million in 10-year securities.

The federal government last week sold the Treasury's new inflation-indexed bonds, which were eagerly snatched up by investors. The bonds make interest payments based on adjustments to the loan amount accounting for inflation.
The authority's inflation-indexed bonds are meant to meet investors' needs for a hedge against inflation, said TVA Chairman Craven Crowell.
"Inflation-indexed bonds represent a new investment opportunity for both individual and institutional investors throughout the world," said TVA Chief Financial Officer David Smith.
Merrill Lynch was the lead manager and sole underwriter for the bond sale. Proceeds from the sale will be used to help retire existing TVA debt.

Created by Congress in 1933, the Tennessee Valley Authority is the nation's largest producer of electricity, providing power to industry and 160 power distributors that serve about 7.3 million consumers in seven southeastern states.
